title: Assertion `buf->b_signcols.count[width - 1] >= 0` failed
body: For the last few days Neovim has sometimes crashed while updating a buffer, for example during undo. The backtrace ends in `buf_signcols_count_range()` with the assertion `buf->b_signcols.count[width - 1] >= 0`. I do not yet know how to reproduce it reliably. I use the 0.10 branch of statuscol and suspected a recent change in `decoration.c`.

symptoms_visible: Neovim occasionally aborts while I update a buffer, for example during undo, with `buf->b_signcols.count[width - 1] >= 0` failing in `buf_signcols_count_range()`.
N0.label: N0 intermittent sign-column assertion reported

symptoms_visible: The assertion is infrequent, and I cannot reproduce it with the Noice command that crashes another setup.
N1.label: N1 sign configuration and frequency described

symptoms_visible: I initially stopped seeing the crash after updating, but the same assertion later occurred again on master while editing.
N1_x.label: N1_x crash recurred after interim change

symptoms_visible: With a reduced sign and extmark setup, deleting text and then removing a sign reliably reaches the same assertion.
N2.label: N2 deletion reproducer obtained

symptoms_visible: The reduced deletion sequence still aborts when a sign is removed.
N3.label: N3 sign-count bookkeeping failure diagnosed

symptoms_visible: After I updated to the latest Nightly, saving no longer triggers the assertion on my affected setup.
N_terminal.label: terminal latest Nightly verified

question_patterns: How are signs and diagnostics configured in the affected setup?
Can you share the relevant sign or diagnostic configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My diagnostic signs use Unicode characters, and I replace the diagnostic signs handler with the documented example pattern so that only the highest-severity diagnostic is shown on each line. I also use statuscol to display the signs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I use different Unicode glyphs, but the same custom diagnostic handler and statuscol setup.
My floating diagnostic window has a square border instead of a rounded one.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the assertion consistently, and what exact action happens immediately before it?
Does the Noice command sequence reported by another affected user reproduce it for you?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I do not get the failure often, and it is difficult to remember the exact edit immediately before the crash. I have Noice installed, but that command does not reproduce the crash with my configuration.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes every time in a clean configuration with no plugins as soon as I open any file.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1, c4, c6 and c7: the original reporter supplied the custom diagnostic handler and explained that the crash was rare and the Noice-specific sequence did not reproduce on their setup.

solution.intent: Apply the interim guard change intended to prevent the sign-column counter from reaching the assertion.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a build containing #27047 and observe whether the assertion returns.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c9 and c13, with corroboration from wookayin in c10: the crash initially appeared absent after #27047 but later recurred, so that change was not a complete resolution.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a configuration and edit sequence that reliably reaches the assertion?
Please provide an exact reproducer showing how signs are placed, text is deleted, and a sign is removed.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reduced it to a small configuration that places sign extmarks and highlight extmarks on several lines. After deleting a large range of text, removing another sign reaches the same assertion reliably.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reduced setup never crashes when text or signs are deleted; it only crashes while an unrelated search plugin opens a window.
The same reduced sequence reproduces, but I need to repeat the deletion twice before it crashes.

edges.comment: Affected user bassamsdata supplied the reproducible configuration in c15; all affected users are folded into one simulated user side. The answer preserves only the actions and observed assertion, while the interpretation of the sign counts remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Correct sign-column bookkeeping after text deletion so marktree traversal counts only the signs actually present and later sign removal cannot decrement the wrong count below zero.
solution.concrete_example: Use the reduced deletion case as a regression test: after deleting the lines, the screen state and sign-column counts must contain only the surviving signs before any callback removes another sign.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainer analysis in c16-c17 established that immediately after deleting text, marktree iteration counted more paired signs than were actually present. That incremented the wrong `b_signcols.count` bucket; a subsequent callback removed a real sign and decremented the correct bucket below zero. These conclusions were derived from the reproducer, not supplied by the affected user.

edges.comment: Maintainer messages c16-c17: luukvbaal reproduced the crash, analyzed the inconsistent post-deletion sign count, and wrote a focused test case.

question_patterns: Please try the newest available build and tell me whether the same save or edit action still triggers the assertion.
Can you install the newest available build, repeat the action that was crashing, and report what you see?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had the assertion again on save with `v0.12.0-dev-571+g7aafbca510`. After updating to `v0.12.0-dev-630+g8af2aea24f`, I could no longer reproduce it. It seems fixed for me.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The newest available build still crashes with the same assertion every time I save.
The newest available build no longer crashes during undo, although my original trigger was editing rather than saving.

solution.intent: Update to a current Neovim Nightly containing the recent assertion-related correction, then verify the original save, undo, or sign-removal trigger before declaring the crash resolved.
solution.concrete_example: A maintainer asked the affected user to try the latest Nightly because a very recent change adjusted this assertion; the user then reported that the newer Nightly no longer reproduced the save-time crash.

edges.comment: Final exchange c33-c35: a later affected user, fm39hz, reported the same assertion during save; bfredl requested a test of the latest Nightly due to a recent assertion adjustment, and that user confirmed the newer build no longer reproduced it. This is folded affected-user verification, not a claim that the opening reporter personally performed the final retest.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the technical failure as inconsistent placed-sign/sign-column bookkeeping: after text deletion the marktree path can count more paired signs than are actually present, and a later sign removal decrements the correct count below zero, triggering the assertion.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected sign/extmark deletion reproducer and the extmark-removal backtrace, not attributed to diagnostic glyphs, statuscol rendering, Noice, or another plugin merely because those components expose the faulty sign operations.
Must not treat the earlier interim guard as a complete fix, because the same assertion recurred after that update.
The resolution should be a current build containing the sign-count/assertion correction, with the affected save, undo, or sign-removal sequence retested.
Must not declare the issue resolved until an affected user verifies that the assertion no longer occurs on a build containing the correction.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically experienced Neovim user who can share Lua configuration, read native backtraces, test development builds, and reduce plugin-dependent behavior; additional affected users contribute progressively smaller reproducers and final Nightly verification.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise, candid when reproduction is unreliable, willing to paste configuration and test updates, and appreciative of maintainer investigation.
